questions.question:
You have just been hired by a company new to Scrum. Your management has assigned you to be the Scrum Master of six new Scrum Teams. These teams will build one product. Select two conditions you should strive for in this scenario.
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: There should be six Product Owners, one for each Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: A product has a single Product Owner, whatever the number of Scrum Teams.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There should be six Product Owners, reporting to a chief Product Owner.
choices.explanation: A chief Product Owner with team Product Owners is not Scrum: one product has one Product Owner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The product has one Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: All Scrum Teams working on the same product share one Product Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Each Scrum Team should have a separate Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Separate Product Backlogs fragment the work and hide dependencies; one product has one Product Backlog.

choices.label: E
choices.text: There should be only one Product Owner.
choices.explanation: One product has one Product Owner, accountable for the single Product Backlog.

questions.question:
A Scrum Team has been working on a product for nine Sprints. A new Product Owner comes in, understanding he is accountable for the Product Backlog. However, he is unsure about his responsibilities. Which two activities are part of the Product Owner role according to Scrum?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ensuring that the most valuable functionality is produced first, at all times.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner orders the Product Backlog so that the most valuable work is done first.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Interacting with stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Engaging stakeholders is part of the Product Owner's work to maximize value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Providing the Scrum Team with detailed specifications.
choices.explanation: Detailed specifications are not required; Product Backlog items are refined collaboratively with the Developers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Describing features as Use Cases.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not prescribe Use Cases; the format of Product Backlog items is free.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Creating detailed functional test cases.
choices.explanation: Test cases are part of the Developers' work to meet the Definition of Done.

questions.question:
User documentation is part of your Definition of Done. However, there aren't enough technical writers for all teams. Your Developers don't have a technical writer. What should you do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Form a separate team of technical writers that will work on an on-demand basis for the various Product Owners. Work order will be first in, first out.
choices.explanation: A separate team working first in, first out creates dependencies and delays; documentation is part of Done.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Let the user documentation remain undone and accumulate until after the last development Sprint. It will then be done by any available technical writers.
choices.explanation: Accumulating undone work hides the real state of the product and violates the Definition of Done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wait until you have a technical writer on your Scrum Team to take care of this.
choices.explanation: Waiting creates undone work; the Scrum Team must meet its Definition of Done now.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Your Scrum Team is still responsible for creating user documentation. In this case, the Scrum Team members will write it.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team remains accountable for meeting the Definition of Done, so its members write the documentation themselves.

questions.question:
You are the Scrum Master for four Scrum Teams working from the same Product Backlog. Several of the Developers come to you complaining that work identified for the upcoming two Sprints will require full-time commitment from a technical specialist who is external to the teams. What are two key concerns for the Scrum Master to take into account in this situation?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The desire to maintain a stable velocity.
choices.explanation: Velocity is not a goal; it is at best a planning indicator, not something to preserve for its own sake.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The benefit of Developers figuring out a solution for themselves.
choices.explanation: Self-managing Developers are best placed to find a solution to the dependency, for example sharing knowledge or adapting the work.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The need to have enough work to keep all Developers busy.
choices.explanation: Keeping people busy is not a goal of Scrum; delivering value is.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ability of the Developers to produce integrated Increments.
choices.explanation: With several teams on one product, the key concern is still producing an integrated, usable Increment each Sprint.

questions.question:
The Product Backlog is ordered by:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Owner with the most valuable items placed at the top.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner orders the Product Backlog to maximize value; the most valuable items are usually at the top.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Risk, where safer items are at the top, and riskier items are at the bottom.
choices.explanation: Risk can be one input, but ordering is not simply by safety; the goal is value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Items are randomly arranged.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is ordered deliberately, never randomly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Size, where small items are at the top and large items are at the bottom.
choices.explanation: Size is not the ordering criterion; small items are at the top because they are refined, not because they are small.

questions.question:
What happens if the Scrum Team cannot complete its work by the end of the Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Sprint is extended and future Sprints use this new duration.
choices.explanation: Sprints have a fixed length; they are never extended to finish work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Sprint length holds and the Scrum Team continuously learns what is actually possible to do within a Sprint of this length.
choices.explanation: The Sprint length holds; the team learns empirically how much it can achieve in a Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Sprint is extended temporarily. Lessons are taken to ensure it doesn't happen again.
choices.explanation: A Sprint is never extended, even temporarily.

questions.question:
Which topics should be discussed in the Sprint Review?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum process, and how it was used during the Sprint.
choices.explanation: How Scrum was used is a topic for the Sprint Retrospective.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coding and engineering practices.
choices.explanation: Engineering practices are inspected at the Sprint Retrospective.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sprint results.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review inspects the outcome of the Sprint, the Increment, and adapts the Product Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All of the above.
choices.explanation: Since the first two topics belong to the Retrospective, this answer is wrong.

questions.question:
A member of the Scrum Team takes the Scrum Master aside to express his concerns about data security issues. What should the Scrum Master do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add security to the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not decide alone; the team should first discuss the concern.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tell the Product Owner to stop further development of features until the issues are fixed.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not order the Product Owner to stop development.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a Product Backlog item for security.
choices.explanation: Creating a Product Backlog item may be an outcome, but the team must first be aware of the issue.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Go check with the testers.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no tester role; quality and security are the Scrum Team's responsibility.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ask the person to share the issue with the team as soon as possible.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master encourages transparency and self-management: the team, informed, decides how to address it.

questions.question:
What does it mean for a Scrum Team to be cross-functional?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Team includes not only Developers but also business analysts, architects, and testers.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no business analyst, architect or tester roles in the team; there are only Developers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Team includes cross-skilled individuals who are able to contribute to do what is necessary to deliver an Increment of software.
choices.explanation: Cross-functional teams have all the skills necessary to create value each Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Developers on the Scrum Team work closely with business analysts, architects, Developers and testers who are not on the team.
choices.explanation: Depending on people outside the team means the team is not cross-functional.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Team is a virtual team drawing from separate teams of business analysts, architects, Developers and testers.
choices.explanation: A virtual team drawn from separate functional teams is not a cross-functional Scrum Team.

questions.question:
Sprint burndown charts are an efficient tracking tool, because they show:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: An estimate of the total work remaining for the Sprint.
choices.explanation: A Sprint burndown shows the estimated work remaining in the Sprint over time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: How much effort has gone into a Sprint.
choices.explanation: Effort spent is not what matters; remaining work is.

choices.label: C
choices.text: How many hours have been worked by each Scrum Team member.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not track individual hours.

choices.label: D
choices.text: How many Product Backlog items remain.
choices.explanation: The number of Product Backlog items remaining is shown by a release or product burndown, not a Sprint burndown.

questions.question:
If burndown charts are used to visualize progress, what does a trend line through a release burndown chart indicate?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The evolution of the cost spent on the project.
choices.explanation: Burndown charts track work remaining, not cost.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When all work will be completed to the Scrum Team can be released for other work.
choices.explanation: A trend line forecasts completion, it is not about releasing the team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the work remaining will likely be completed if nothing changes on the Product Backlog or the Developers.
choices.explanation: The trend projects when the remaining work will be done, assuming nothing changes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the project will be over if the Product Owner removes work that is equal in effort to any new work that is added.
choices.explanation: The trend line does not assume that new work will be compensated by removing equivalent work.

questions.question:
Who is responsible for engaging the stakeholders?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Business Analyst.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no business analyst role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers may collaborate with stakeholders, but engaging them is the Product Owner's responsibility.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Team Manager.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no team manager role.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Project Manager.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no project manager role.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner represents the needs of stakeholders and engages with them.

questions.question:
At the end of a Sprint, a Product Backlog item worked on during the Sprint does not meet the Definition of Done. What two things should happen with the undone Product Backlog item?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the stakeholders agree, the Product Owner can accept it and release it to the users.
choices.explanation: Items that do not meet the Definition of Done cannot be accepted or released regardless of stakeholder agreement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Put it on the Product Backlog for the Product Owner to decide what to do with it.
choices.explanation: Any Product Backlog item that does not meet the Definition of Done cannot be part of the Increment and is returned to the Product Backlog for re-ordering.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Review the item, add the Done part of the estimate to the velocity and create a Story for the remaining work.
choices.explanation: Velocity is not partially counted for incomplete items; work not meeting the Definition of Done is not included.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Do not include the item in the Increment this Sprint.
choices.explanation: An item that does not meet the Definition of Done cannot be part of the Increment for that Sprint.

questions.question:
Which two of the following are true about the Scrum Master role?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the Sprint Review, the Scrum Master identifies what has been "done" and what has not been "done".
choices.explanation: Done is defined by the Definition of Done, not judged by the Scrum Master at the Sprint Review.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Master teaches the Developers to keep the Scrum meetings to their time-box.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master ensures events are productive and kept within the timebox.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Master helps those outside the team interact with the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master helps those outside the Scrum Team understand which interactions are helpful.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master assigns tasks to Developers when they need work.
choices.explanation: Developers self-manage and pick their own work; the Scrum Master does not assign tasks.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Scrum Master is responsible for updating the Sprint Burndown.
choices.explanation: Developers track their own progress; the Scrum Master is not responsible for a burndown.

questions.question:
What are three benefits of self-management?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased creativity.
choices.explanation: Autonomy encourages people to find new and better solutions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased rule compliance.
choices.explanation: Self-management is not about compliance with rules; it is about autonomy over who does what, when and how.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased accuracy of estimates.
choices.explanation: Estimates are not necessarily more accurate; uncertainty remains in complex work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased self-accountability
choices.explanation: Self-managing teams own their work and feel more accountable for the outcome.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased commitment.
choices.explanation: People who decide how to do their work are more committed to it.

questions.question:
Which three of the following are time-boxed events in Scrum?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Release Testing.
choices.explanation: Release Testing is not a Scrum event.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Release Retrospective.
choices.explanation: There is no Release Retrospective in Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sprint Retrospective.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is timeboxed to three hours for a one-month Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sprint Planning.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is timeboxed to eight hours for a one-month Sprint.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sprint Testing.
choices.explanation: There is no testing Sprint in Scrum.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Sprint 0.
choices.explanation: Sprint 0 does not exist in Scrum.

choices.label: G
choices.text: Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is timeboxed to 15 minutes.

questions.question:
What is the best suited structure for Scrum Teams in order to produce integrated Increments?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Each Scrum Team works only one technical layer of the system (e.g. GUI, database, middle tier, interfaces).
choices.explanation: Component teams by layer create dependencies and delay integration.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Each Scrum Team develops functionality from beginning to end throughout all technical layers.
choices.explanation: Feature teams develop end-to-end functionality across all layers and produce integrated Increments.

questions.question:
Why should the Product Owner be present at the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: He/She doesn't need to be there.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is for the Developers; the Product Owner is not required.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To hear about impediments in functionality.
choices.explanation: Impediments are raised by the Developers; the Product Owner does not need to be present.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To represent the stakeholder's point of view.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is not about stakeholders.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To participate as a Scrum Team member.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner only participates as a Developer if actively working on Sprint Backlog items.

questions.question:
What two techniques could the Scrum Master use when the Scrum Team gets caught in an internal disagreement about which development techniques to apply?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Involve the complete Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Involving the whole Scrum Team supports self-management and shared ownership of the decision.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use coaching techniques; such as open questions and active listening.
choices.explanation: Coaching techniques help the team resolve its own conflict.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ask an external technical specialist to make the decision.
choices.explanation: Imposing an external decision undermines self-management.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Send every team member to the company's Human Resources department to express their concerns.
choices.explanation: Escalating to HR is inappropriate for a technical disagreement.

questions.question:
What enhances the transparency of an Increment?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Doing all work needed to meet the Definition of Done
choices.explanation: Meeting the Definition of Done makes it clear what has really been completed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reporting Sprint progress to the stakeholders daily
choices.explanation: Daily reporting is not what creates transparency over the Increment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keeping track of and estimating all undone work to be completed in a separate Sprint.
choices.explanation: Undone work in a separate Sprint hides the real state of the product.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Updating Sprint tasks properly in the electronic tracking tool.
choices.explanation: Updating tools does not guarantee transparency of the Increment.

questions.question:
Who determines how work is performed during the Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Architects.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no architect role deciding how work is done.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The self-managing Scrum Team internally decides who does what, when and how.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not decide how work is performed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Subject matter experts.
choices.explanation: Experts may advise, but they do not decide.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Developers' managers.
choices.explanation: Managers do not decide how the Scrum Team works.

questions.question:
When does the second Sprint start?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Once the architectural changes for the second Sprint have been approved by the senior architect.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not depend on external architectural approval to start a Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: After the Product Backlog for the second Sprint has been selected.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning occurs at the start of the Sprint, not before it officially begins.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immediately after the first Sprint.
choices.explanation: A new Sprint starts immediately after the previous Sprint ends.

choices.label: D
choices.text: After the customer completes acceptance testing of the first Sprint.
choices.explanation: Sprint transitions are not dependent on customer acceptance testing.

questions.question:
What is included in the Sprint Backlog?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: User Stories.
choices.explanation: User Stories can be part of the Sprint Backlog, but not exclusively.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tasks.
choices.explanation: Tasks can be part of the Sprint Backlog, but not exclusively.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Cases.
choices.explanation: Use Cases can be used, but not exclusively.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tests.
choices.explanation: Tests can be part of the plan, but not exclusively.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any of the above (or others) which are a decomposition of the selected Product Backlog items.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog contains whatever decomposition the Developers find useful.

questions.question:
Which of the following are true about the Product Owner role?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Owner is one person.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is one person, not a committee.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner is accountable for ordering the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for Product Backlog management, including ordering.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Multiple people can share the Product Owner role on a Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner role is not shared; it is one person.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner role can be played by a committee or a team of people.
choices.explanation: A committee cannot be Product Owner; it is one person.

questions.question: True or False: When multiple teams work together on the same product, each team should maintain a separate Product Backlog.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Multiple teams on one product share one Product Backlog.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: A single product has a single Product Backlog.

questions.question:
If two Scrum Teams are added to the development of a product that previously had only one Scrum Team, what will be the immediate impact on the productivity of the original Scrum Team?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Its productivity is likely to decrease.
choices.explanation: Adding teams creates onboarding and coordination overhead; productivity of the original team often decreases first.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Its productivity is likely to stay the same.
choices.explanation: The original team must help onboard and coordinate, which affects productivity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its productivity is likely to increase.
choices.explanation: Productivity rarely increases immediately when teams are added.

questions.question:
A Scrum Master is introducing Scrum to a new Scrum Team. The Scrum Team has decided that a Sprint Retrospective is unnecessary. What action should the Scrum Master take?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Call a meeting between the Scrum Team and senior management.
choices.explanation: Escalating to management is not the first action; the Scrum Master teaches Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Comply with the decision of the self-managing team.
choices.explanation: Self-management happens within Scrum; the Sprint Retrospective is mandatory.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Consult with the Product Owner to see how he/she feels about the situation.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective concerns the whole Scrum Team; the Product Owner's opinion does not change that it is mandatory.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Begin facilitating productive and useful Sprint Retrospectives.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master ensures that all Scrum events take place and are positive and productive.

questions.question:
Which two things are appropriate for a Scrum Master to do if the Developers don't have the engineering tools and infrastructure to completely finish each selected Product Backlog item?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coach the Scrum Team to improve its skills, tools, and infrastructure over time and adjust the Definition of Done accordingly.
choices.explanation: Over time the team should improve its capabilities and strengthen its Definition of Done.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Encourage the Product Owner to accept partially "Done" Increments until the situation improves.
choices.explanation: Partially done Increments are not Increments; work that does not meet the Definition of Done cannot be released.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Refocus the current Sprint on establishing the Scrum Team's infrastructure instead of delivering an Increment.
choices.explanation: Every Sprint must produce a usable Increment; the environment should improve alongside the work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Declare the Scrum Team not ready for Scrum.
choices.explanation: Scrum is meant to be adopted progressively; teams do not need to be 'ready'.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Have the Scrum Team establish a Definition of Done that is actually possible to achieve given current circumstances.
choices.explanation: A Definition of Done that is achievable now keeps transparency on what Done really means.

questions.question:
When is implementation of a Product Backlog item considered complete?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the end of the Sprint.
choices.explanation: The end of the Sprint does not make work Done.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the item has no work remaining in order to be potentially released.
choices.explanation: An item is complete when it meets the Definition of Done, with no work remaining before it could be released.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When QA reports that the item passes all acceptance criteria.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no separate QA; Done is defined by the Definition of Done.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When all work in the Sprint Backlog related to the item is finished.
choices.explanation: Finishing the tasks is not enough if the Definition of Done is not met.

questions.question:
Choose two responsibilities of a self-managing Scrum Team.
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reorder the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Reordering the Product Backlog is the Product Owner's accountability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pull Product Backlog items for the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Developers select the Product Backlog items for the Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Do the work planned in the Sprint Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team does the work planned in the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase velocity.
choices.explanation: Velocity is not a goal.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Report daily progress to stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Daily reporting to stakeholders is not a Scrum responsibility.

questions.question:
Every Scrum Team should have:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least one representative from each major software engineering discipline (like QA, Dev, UX).
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require representatives of disciplines; it requires the necessary skills.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The competencies and skills needed to deliver a Done Increment in a Sprint.
choices.explanation: Every Scrum Team should be cross-functional, with all skills needed to create a valuable Increment each Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: One Lead Developer and no more than 8 other members.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Lead Developer.

questions.question:
Why does the Product Owner want the Scrum Team to adhere to its Definition of Done?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: To have complete transparency into what has been done at the end of each Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done creates transparency about the state of the Increment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To be able to reprimand the team when they don't meet their velocity goal for the Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done is not used to measure velocity or reprimand the team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To know what the team will deliver over the next three Sprints.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done does not determine future Sprint delivery.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To predict the team's productivity over time.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done ensures quality and transparency, not productivity prediction.

questions.question:
During a Sprint Retrospective, for what is the Scrum Master responsible?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prioritizing the resulting action items.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team prioritizes its own improvements.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Participating as a Scrum team member and facilitating as requested or needed.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master participates as a team member and facilitates when needed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acting as a scribe to capture the Developers' answers.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is not a scribe.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Summarizing and reporting the discussions to management.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective is not a reporting meeting for management.

questions.question:
During the Sprint, the Scrum Master's role is to do which two of the following:
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Facilitate inspection and adaptation opportunities as requested or needed.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master facilitates inspection and adaptation opportunities as needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coaching the team members in the self-management.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master coaches the team members in self-management and cross-functionality.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ensure the Product Owner attends all Scrum events.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner's attendance is not something the Scrum Master enforces.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Escalate team conflicts to functional line managers.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master helps resolve conflicts; escalation is not the default.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Monitor the progress of the Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers monitor their own progress.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Assign tasks with the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not assign tasks.

questions.question:
The Scrum Master observes the Product Owner struggling with ordering the Product Backlog. What is an appropriate action for the Scrum Master to take?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Suggest the Product Owner extend the Sprint, so he can have more time to order the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Sprints are never extended.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Suggest that the Developers do the ordering to be sure that it is a feasible ordering of work.
choices.explanation: Ordering is the Product Owner's accountability; the Developers can advise but do not own it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Offer the Product Owner help in understanding that the goal of ordering the Product Backlog is to maximize value.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master serves the Product Owner by helping them understand that ordering aims to maximize value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Present the Product Owner with an ordered Product Backlog to use.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master helps, but must not take over the Product Owner's accountability.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Encourage the Product Owner to work with the Developers to see which items technically are fastest to implement.
choices.explanation: Technical speed is not the goal of ordering; value is.

questions.question:
Which statement best describes the Sprint Review?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is used to congratulate the Developers if it did what it forecast, or to punish the Developers if it failed to meet its forecast.
choices.explanation: It is not about praise or punishment; it is a working session.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a demo at the end of the Sprint for everyone in the organization to check on the work done.
choices.explanation: It should not be limited to a demo; it is a collaborative working session.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a mechanism to control the Developers' activities during a Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review is not a control mechanism.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is when the Scrum Team and stakeholders inspect the outcome of a Sprint and figure out what to do next.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review is where the Scrum Team presents results to key stakeholders and together they discuss progress and what to do next.

questions.question:
When might a Sprint be abnormally cancelled?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the Scrum Team feels that the work is too hard.
choices.explanation: Difficulty is not a reason to cancel; the scope can be renegotiated.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
choices.explanation: A Sprint may be cancelled when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the sales department has an important new opportunity.
choices.explanation: A new opportunity can be added to the Product Backlog; it does not justify cancellation unless the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When it becomes clear that not everything will be finished by the end of the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Not finishing everything is handled by renegotiating scope, not by cancelling.

questions.question:
A Sprint Retrospective should be held:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the end of each Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective concludes each Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the beginning of each Sprint.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning starts the Sprint, not the Retrospective.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only when the Scrum Team determines it needs one.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective is mandatory every Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At the end of the last Sprint in a project or a release.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective happens every Sprint, not only at the end of a project.

questions.question:
A new Developer is having continuing conflicts with existing Developers and creating the hostile environment. If necessary, who is responsible for removing the team member?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hiring manager is responsible, because he/she hired the Developer.
choices.explanation: Hiring managers are outside the team; the self-managing team handles its composition issues.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Manager is responsible, because he/she removes Impediments.
choices.explanation: There is no Scrum Manager in Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers are responsible, and may need help from the Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The self-managing Developers handle their composition issues, with help from the Scrum Master if needed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner is responsible, because he/she controls the return on investment (ROI).
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is not responsible for team composition.

questions.question:
During a Sprint Retrospective, the Developers propose moving the Daily Scrum to only occur on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Which two are the most appropriate responses for the Scrum Master?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consider the request and decide on which days the Daily Scrum should occur.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not decide on the Developers' behalf.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coach the team on why the Daily Scrum is important as an opportunity to update the plan.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master should explain why the Daily Scrum matters: it is the daily opportunity to inspect progress and adapt the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have the Developers vote.
choices.explanation: Voting does not address the underlying reason and could remove a mandatory event.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Learn why the Developers want this and work with them to improve the outcome of the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: Understanding the root cause helps the team improve the Daily Scrum rather than abandon it.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Acknowledge and support the self-managing team's decision.
choices.explanation: Self-management works within the Scrum framework; skipping Daily Scrums removes an inspection and adaptation opportunity.

questions.question:
When should a Sprint Goal be created?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: It should have been created in the previous Sprint during Product Backlog refinement.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Goal is crafted during Sprint Planning, not before.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It must be established before Sprint Planning in order to begin planning.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Goal is defined during Sprint Planning, not as a prerequisite.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A Sprint Goal is not mandatory in Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Goal is mandatory; it is the commitment of the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At any time during the Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Goal is set at Sprint Planning and stays stable during the Sprint.

choices.label: E
choices.text: During Sprint Planning.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team crafts the Sprint Goal during Sprint Planning.

questions.question: True or False: Every Scrum team must have a Product Owner and Scrum Master.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True. Outcomes affected by their participation and availability.
choices.explanation: A Scrum Team consists of one Scrum Master, one Product Owner and Developers; how much they engage affects outcomes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False. A Product Owner can be replaced by a business analyst in the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is one person and cannot be replaced by a Business Analyst.

choices.label: C
choices.text: False. A Scrum Master is only required when asked for by the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is a required accountability of every Scrum Team, not an optional one.

choices.label: D
choices.text: True. Each must be 100% dedicated to the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require 100% dedication; what matters is their participation and availability.

questions.question:
Who can abnormally terminate a Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master cannot cancel a Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Team or its members.
choices.explanation: The Developers cannot cancel a Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders cannot cancel a Sprint; they can influence the Product Owner.

questions.question: True or False: The Sprint Goal is a result of Sprint Planning, as is the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning produces the Sprint Goal and the Sprint Backlog, which includes the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Both the Sprint Goal and the Sprint Backlog are created during Sprint Planning.

questions.question:
Which two of the following are appropriate topics for discussion during a Sprint Retrospective?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Identifying high priority process improvements for the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective identifies the most helpful process improvements.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The order of items in the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Ordering the Product Backlog is for the Product Owner, typically outside the Retrospective.

choices.label: C
choices.text: How the team collaborates.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective inspects how individuals, interactions and processes worked.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Documenting acceptance criteria for items in the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: Acceptance criteria are refined during Product Backlog refinement.

questions.question:
A Scrum Master is working with a Scrum Team that has members in different physical locations. The Scrum Team meets in a variety of meeting rooms and has much to do logistically (for example, set up conference calls) before the Daily Scrum. What action should the Scrum Master take?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allow the Scrum Team to self-manage and determine for itself what to do.
choices.explanation: The Developers self-manage logistics; they can find their own solution.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set up the meeting and tell the Scrum Team that is how it will be done.
choices.explanation: Imposing a solution undermines self-management.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ask the Scrum Team members to alternate who is responsible for meeting setup.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master should not impose a solution, even a rotation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inform management and ask them to solve it.
choices.explanation: Escalating a team-level logistic issue removes autonomy.

questions.question: True or False: Cross-functional teams are optimized to work on one technical layer of a system only (e.g. GUI, database, middle tier, interfaces).

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Cross-functional teams have all skills needed to create value across all layers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Working on a single layer is the opposite of cross-functionality; it creates dependencies.

questions.question:
Which of the following might the Scrum Team discuss during a Sprint Retrospective?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Methods of communication.
choices.explanation: Communication is part of individuals and interactions, a valid topic but not the only one.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The way the Scrum Team does Sprint Planning.
choices.explanation: How events are run is part of process improvements, but not the only valid topic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skills needed to improve the Developers' ability to deliver.
choices.explanation: Skills and tools are inspected at the Retrospective, but they are not the only topic.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Its Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done is inspected at the Retrospective, but other topics are valid too.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All of the above.
choices.explanation: All of these are valid Retrospective topics: individuals, interactions, processes, tools and the Definition of Done.

questions.question:
You are the Scrum Master of a new, to be developed product. Development is going to require 45 people. What is a good first question for you to suggest the group thinks about when forming into teams?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: How will we make sure all teams have the right amount of expertise?
choices.explanation: Each team needs all the skills necessary to create a valuable Increment each Sprint (cross-functional teams).

choices.label: B
choices.text: What is the right mixture of senior and junior people on each team?
choices.explanation: Seniority mix is secondary; what matters is having the skills to create value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Who are going to be the team leads?
choices.explanation: There are no team leads in Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Who are the subject matter experts on each team?
choices.explanation: Scrum has no specialist subject-matter-expert roles in teams.

questions.question:
Which three of the following are feedback loops in Scrum?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sprint Review.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review inspects the Increment with stakeholders and adapts the Product Backlog.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Release Planning.
choices.explanation: Release Planning is not a Scrum event.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sprint Retrospective.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective inspects how the Scrum Team works and plans improvements.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refinement Meeting.
choices.explanation: Refinement is an ongoing activity, not a formal feedback loop event of Scrum.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum inspects progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapts the Sprint Backlog.

questions.question:
When the Developers are having trouble delivering a working Increment because they don't understand a functional requirement, what should they do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a specialist to the Developers.
choices.explanation: Adding people is not the first response to a misunderstanding.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Partially complete the functionality, and discuss the remaining work at the Sprint Review.
choices.explanation: Partially done work is not part of the Increment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Collaborate with the Product Owner to determine what is possible and acceptable.
choices.explanation: Deferring work does not solve the misunderstanding.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Defer the work to a more appropriate Sprint.
choices.explanation: Developers collaborate with the Product Owner to find what is possible and acceptable.

questions.question:
When is the Sprint Backlog created?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the beginning of the project.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog is created per Sprint, not at the start of a project.

choices.label: B
choices.text: During the Sprint Planning meeting.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog is created during Sprint Planning.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prior to the Sprint Planning meeting.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog does not exist before Sprint Planning.

choices.label: D
choices.text: During the Sprint.
choices.explanation: It is created at Sprint Planning, then updated during the Sprint.

questions.question:
Which of the following services are appropriate for a Scrum Master in regard to the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lead the discussions of the Developers.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is for and by the Developers; the Scrum Master does not lead it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Make sure that all 3 questions have been answered by each member of the team.
choices.explanation: The three questions are no longer required in Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keep track of whether each team member has a chance to speak.
choices.explanation: Monitoring who speaks is not the Scrum Master's role; the Developers self-manage the event.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Teach the Developers to keep the Daily Scrum within the 15 minute time-box.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master ensures events are kept within the timebox, for example by teaching the Developers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All of the above.
choices.explanation: Since the other options are not appropriate, this answer cannot be correct.

questions.question:
In order to achieve the benefits of Scrum, it is important to enact the value of commitment. What two actions demonstrate the commitment of Scrum Team members?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Always deliver the items in the Sprint forecast.
choices.explanation: A forecast is not a guarantee; commitment is about effort and goals, not delivering everything.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Help the other Scrum Team members.
choices.explanation: Helping others shows commitment to the team's goals.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Do your best
choices.explanation: Doing one's best shows personal commitment to achieving the goals of the Scrum Team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Send out a daily status report.
choices.explanation: Status reports do not demonstrate commitment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Work late.
choices.explanation: Working late is not sustainable and is not what commitment means.

questions.question: True or False: The Product Owner determines how many Product Backlog items the Developers select for a Sprint.

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Only the Developers decide how much work they select for a Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True, accordingly to what was committed to the stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Stakeholder commitments do not dictate how much the Developers select.

choices.label: C
choices.text: True, but only after confirmation by the resource manager that the Team has enough capacity.
choices.explanation: There is no resource manager deciding capacity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not decide how much work the Developers take.

choices.label: E
choices.text: False, the Scrum Master does that.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not decide; the Developers do.

choices.label: F
choices.text: False, capacity and commitment are the Project manager's responsibility.
choices.explanation: There is no Project Manager in Scrum; the Developers decide.

questions.question:
What are two ways that regulatory compliance requirements are dealt with in Scrum?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are addressed by a separate team who is responsible for compliance issues.
choices.explanation: Compliance is the Scrum Team's responsibility, not a separate team's.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are discussed, analyzed, and documented before the first Sprint can begin.
choices.explanation: Requirements emerge; nothing must be fully documented before the first Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are added to the Product Backlog and addressed during each Sprint, alongside the creation of new Product capabilities.
choices.explanation: Compliance items can be added to the Product Backlog and addressed Sprint after Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are addressed as part of meeting the Definition of Done during each Sprint.
choices.explanation: Compliance requirements that apply to every Increment can be part of the Definition of Done.

questions.question:
The Sprint Review is mainly an inspect and adapt opportunity for which group?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers and stakeholders.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is also part of the Sprint Review.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner and Developers.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders are key participants in the Sprint Review.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Team and stakeholders.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review is a working session of the Scrum Team and stakeholders.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner and management.
choices.explanation: Management is not specifically the audience; stakeholders are, with the whole Scrum Team.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Developers and management.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner and the Scrum Master also participate.

choices.label: F
choices.text: The Product Owner and stakeholders.
choices.explanation: The whole Scrum Team participates, not only the Product Owner.

questions.question: True or False: To get started in terms of what to build, Scrum requires no more than a Product Owner with enough ideas for a first Sprint, Developers to implement those ideas and a Scrum Master to help guide the process.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Scrum needs only a Product Owner with enough ideas, Developers and a Scrum Master to start; the Product Backlog emerges.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require a complete Product Backlog to start.

questions.question: True or False: A product Increment must be released to production at the end of each Sprint.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Releasing is a Product Owner decision; it is not mandatory every Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: An Increment must be usable, but whether to release it is a business decision.

questions.question:
How is management external to the Scrum Team involved in the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master speaks on their behalf.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not represent management at the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Team self-manages and is the only management required at the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Developers self-manage; the Daily Scrum is their event.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Management gives an update at the start of each Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: Management does not give updates at the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner represents their opinions.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not represent management at the Daily Scrum.

questions.question:
A Scrum Master is keeping a list of open impediments, but it is growing and he/she has been able to resolve only a small portion of the impediments. Which three techniques would be most helpful in this situation?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consulting with the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Consulting the Scrum Team helps solve impediments together, and the team may resolve some itself.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prioritizing the list and working on them in order.
choices.explanation: Prioritizing the list helps tackle the most impactful impediments first.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Arranging a triage meeting with all project managers.
choices.explanation: There are no project managers in Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Alerting management to the impediments and their impact.
choices.explanation: Making management aware of impediments and their impact helps remove organizational impediments.

questions.question:
Which Scrum Value is affected by a lack of trust in the Scrum Team?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Focus.
choices.explanation: Focus is affected, but it is not the only value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Respect.
choices.explanation: Respect is affected, but it is not the only value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Openness.
choices.explanation: Openness is affected, but it is not the only value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Courage.
choices.explanation: Courage is affected, but it is not the only value.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Commitment.
choices.explanation: Commitment is affected, but it is not the only value.

choices.label: F
choices.text: All of the above.
choices.explanation: Trust underpins all five Scrum values; a lack of trust affects all of them.

questions.question:
What is a Scrum Team responsible for?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Resolving internal team conflicts.
choices.explanation: A self-managing team resolves its internal conflicts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reporting productivity.
choices.explanation: Reporting productivity is not a Scrum responsibility.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Selecting the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team does not select the Product Owner.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Organizing the work required to meet the Sprint Goal.
choices.explanation: Developers organize the work required to meet the Sprint Goal.

questions.question:
Which two ways of creating Scrum Teams are consistent with Scrum's values?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Existing teams propose how they would like to go about organizing into the new structure.
choices.explanation: Letting existing teams propose their organization respects self-management and Scrum values.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Managers personally re-assign current subordinates to new teams.
choices.explanation: Imposing assignments goes against self-management.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Managers collaborate to assign individuals to specific teams.
choices.explanation: Managers assigning people is still a top-down decision.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bring all the Developers together and let them self-manage into Scrum Teams.
choices.explanation: Letting people self-organize into teams shows respect and openness.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Chief Product Owner determines the new team structures and assignments.
choices.explanation: A 'chief Product Owner' deciding team structure is top-down and not part of Scrum.

questions.question: True or False: A Scrum Master is essentially the same thing as a traditional PM (Project Manager).

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master serves the team and the organization; they are not a project manager who plans and controls.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not assign work or manage scope; it is a different accountability.

questions.question:
The Product Owner is not collaborating with the Developers during the Sprint. What are two valuable actions for a Scrum Master to take?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inform the Product Owner's functional manager.
choices.explanation: Escalating to a manager is not the first step; coaching is.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stop the Sprint, send the Product Owner to a course and restart.
choices.explanation: Stopping the Sprint is not appropriate; only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bring up the problem in the Sprint Retrospective.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is the right moment to discuss collaboration.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coach the Product Owner in the values of Scrum and incremental delivery.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master coaches the Product Owner on the importance of collaboration and incremental delivery.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nominate a proxy Product Owner.
choices.explanation: A proxy Product Owner is not part of Scrum.

questions.question:
For the purpose of transparency, when does Scrum say a new Increment of working software must be available?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: After the acceptance testing phase.
choices.explanation: There is no separate acceptance testing phase in Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Before the release Sprint.
choices.explanation: Release Sprints do not exist in Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every 3 Sprints.
choices.explanation: An Increment must be available every Sprint, not every three Sprints.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At the end of every Sprint.
choices.explanation: At least one useful Increment is created every Sprint; it may be delivered even earlier.

choices.label: E
choices.text: When the Product Owner asks to create one.
choices.explanation: Creating Increments is not on request; it happens every Sprint.

questions.question: True or False: Multiple Scrum Teams working on the same project must have the same Sprint start date.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Teams on the same product do not need the same Sprint start date, as long as they integrate their work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require the same start date for all teams.

questions.question:
During a Sprint Retrospective, for what is the Product Owner responsible?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Participating as a Scrum Team member.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner participates as a full member of the Scrum Team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Summarizing and reporting the discussions to the stakeholders that he/she represents in the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective is internal to the Scrum Team; it is not a reporting meeting.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Capturing requirements for the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective is not about capturing requirements.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner should not take part in Sprint Retrospectives.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is part of the Scrum Team and takes part in the Retrospective.

questions.question:
The length of a Sprint should be:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Short enough to keep the business risk acceptable to the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: Shorter Sprints limit business risk.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Short enough to be able to synchronize the development work with other business events.
choices.explanation: Sprints can be aligned with business events.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No more than one calendar month.
choices.explanation: Sprints are one month or less.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All of these answers are correct.
choices.explanation: All these considerations apply to choosing the Sprint length.

questions.question:
What are two responsibilities of testers in a Scrum Team?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Verifying the work of programmers.
choices.explanation: There is no role checking other people's work; Developers are collectively accountable for quality.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Everyone in the Developers are responsible for quality.
choices.explanation: The Developers are accountable for instilling quality by adhering to the Definition of Done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tracking quality metrics.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not define specialised roles like Tester; quality is the responsibility of the Developers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Finding bugs.
choices.explanation: Finding bugs is part of the Developers' work, not a separate role in Scrum.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scrum has no "tester" role.
choices.explanation: Scrum only recognizes Developers, the Product Owner and the Scrum Master; there are no Testers as a role.

questions.question:
The CEO asks the Developers to add a "very important" item to a Sprint that is in progress. What should the Developers do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add the item to the current Sprint and drop an item of equal size.
choices.explanation: Only the Product Owner can change scope during a Sprint with the Developers; the CEO should go through the Product Owner.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add the item to the current Sprint without any adjustments.
choices.explanation: Adding work without discussion endangers the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inform the Product Owner so he/she can work with the CEO.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner decides how to handle new requests and works with stakeholders.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add the item to the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: Planning is the Product Owner's decision, not the Developers'.

questions.question:
How much of the Sprint Backlog must be defined during the Sprint Planning event?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Just enough tasks for the Scrum Master to be confident in the Developers' understanding of the Sprint.
choices.explanation: The plan is created for the Developers, not for the Scrum Master.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The entire Sprint Backlog must be identified and estimated by the end of the Sprint Planning meeting.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog emerges during the Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enough so the Developers can create its best forecast of what it can do, and to start the first several days of the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Developers plan enough to forecast what they can do and to start working on the first days.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Just enough to understand design and architectural implications.
choices.explanation: Design implications are part of the plan, but the plan must be enough to forecast the work.

questions.question:
Who is responsible for managing the progress of work during a Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not manage the Developers' work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers manage their own progress during the Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not manage the Developers' work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The most junior member of the Team.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no hierarchy among Developers.

questions.question:
Who is responsible for collaborating with stakeholders?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers collaborate with stakeholders, but not alone.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Team Manager.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Team Manager.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Project Manager.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Project Manager.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team as a whole collaborates with stakeholders.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Business Analyst.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Business Analyst role.

questions.question:
What two factors are best considered when establishing the Sprint length?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The organization has mandated similar length sprints.
choices.explanation: Organizational mandates are not the best reason to choose a Sprint length.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The level of uncertainty over the technology to be used.
choices.explanation: Higher uncertainty calls for shorter Sprints to get feedback more often.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The frequency at which team formation can be changed.
choices.explanation: Team formation changes are not a factor for Sprint length.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The risk of being disconnected from the stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Shorter Sprints reduce the risk of being disconnected from stakeholders.

questions.question:
Which of these may the Developers deliver at the end of a Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Failing unit tests, to identify acceptance tests for the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: Failing tests mean the Increment is not Done.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An Increment of software with minor known bugs in it.
choices.explanation: Known bugs that violate the Definition of Done prevent the work from being Done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An Increment of working software that is "done".
choices.explanation: Developers deliver a usable Increment that meets the Definition of Done.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A single document, if that is what the Scrum Master asked for.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not decide what is delivered.

questions.question:
Who creates a Product Backlog item's estimate?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers after clarifying requirements with the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Developers who will be doing the work are responsible for the sizing; they clarify the items with the Product Owner.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner with input from the Developers.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is not responsible for sizing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The most senior people in the organization, including architects and subject matter experts.
choices.explanation: Seniority does not give estimation responsibility.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not estimate.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Developers, alone.
choices.explanation: Developers size the work, but refinement is collaborative with the Product Owner.

questions.question:
Who starts the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The person coming in last. This encourages people to be on time and helps to stay within the time-box.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not prescribe who starts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whoever the Developers decide should start.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not prescribe a token.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The person who has the token.
choices.explanation: The Developers decide how to run their Daily Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master. This ensures that the Developers have the meeting and stays within the time-box.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not start or run the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The person who last broke the build.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not prescribe who starts.

questions.question:
You are the Scrum Master on a newly formed Scrum Team. Which three of the following activities would probably help the team in starting up?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Introduce a bonus system for the top performers in the team.
choices.explanation: Individual bonuses undermine team collaboration.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have the Scrum Team members introduce themselves to each other and give a brief background of their skills and work history.
choices.explanation: Getting to know each other's skills helps the team form.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have the development managers for each Developer introduce their direct reports and go over their responsibilities on the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Managers presenting their staff undermine self-management.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ensure the Scrum Team members have compatible personalities.
choices.explanation: Personality compatibility is not something the Scrum Master ensures.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ensure the team understands they need a Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: A Definition of Done is needed to create Done Increments.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Ask the Product Owner to discuss the product or project, its history, goals, and context, as well as answer questions.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner shares context and goals so the team understands the product.

questions.question:
The Developers select a set of Product Backlog items for a Sprint Backlog with the intent to get the selected items "Done" by the end of the Sprint. Which three phrases best describe the purpose of a Definition of Done?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: It controls whether the Developers have performed their tasks.
choices.explanation: It is not a control tool over individuals; Developers are self-managing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It provides a template for elements that need to be included in the technical documentation.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done is not a documentation template.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It creates transparency over the work inspected at the Sprint Review.
choices.explanation: It creates transparency by giving everyone a shared understanding of what was completed and is inspected at the Sprint Review.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It tracks the percent completeness of a Product Backlog item.
choices.explanation: Done is binary; the Definition of Done does not track percentages.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It guides the Developers in creating a forecast at the Sprint Planning.
choices.explanation: Knowing what Done means helps the Developers estimate how much work they can take into the Sprint.

choices.label: F
choices.text: It defines what it takes for an Increment to be ready for release.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done describes the quality required for the Increment to be usable and releasable.

questions.question:
The Daily Scrum is an event that happens every day. What would be three key concerns if the frequency were to be lowered to every two or three days?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Opportunities to inspect and adapt the Sprint Backlog are lost.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum exists to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog. Reducing its frequency reduces inspection and adaptation opportunities.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Impediments are raised and resolved more slowly.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum helps surface impediments quickly. Meeting less often delays identifying and addressing them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner cannot accurately report progress to the stakeholders.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is for Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal. It is not primarily for enabling stakeholder reporting.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Too much work is spent updating the Scrum board before the meeting.
choices.explanation: Updating the Scrum board is not the purpose of the Daily Scrum. Lowering the frequency does not directly create extra work for board updates.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Scrum Master loses the ability to update the Gantt chart properly.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require a Gantt chart, and updating one is not tied to the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: F
choices.text: The Sprint Backlog may become inaccurate.
choices.explanation: Without daily inspection, the Sprint Backlog may not reflect current progress or remaining work, leading to inaccuracies.

questions.question:
Which statement best describes Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A defined and predictive process that conforms to the principles of Scientific Management.
choices.explanation: Scrum is empirical, not defined or predictive.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A complete methodology that defines how to develop software.
choices.explanation: Scrum is a framework, not a complete methodology.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A cookbook that defines best practices for software development.
choices.explanation: Scrum is not a cookbook of practices.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A framework within which complex products in complex environments are developed.
choices.explanation: Scrum is a framework within which people address complex problems and deliver valuable products.

questions.question:
Which Scrum Values are exhibited by not building Product Backlog items that have low business value?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Economic Value Added.
choices.explanation: Economic Value Added is a financial metric, not a Scrum value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Respect.
choices.explanation: Respecting users and stakeholders means not wasting their money on low-value work.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Focus.
choices.explanation: Focus means working on what matters most.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Earned Value.
choices.explanation: Earned Value is a project-management concept, not a Scrum value.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Courage.
choices.explanation: Courage is needed to say no to low-value work.

questions.question:
How should Product Backlog items be chosen when multiple Scrum Teams work from the same Product Backlog?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Team with the highest velocity pulls Product Backlog items first.
choices.explanation: Velocity does not decide who pulls work first.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers pull in work in agreement with the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: Developers pull work from the shared Product Backlog in agreement with the Product Owner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner should provide each team with its own Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: One product has one Product Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Each Scrum Team takes an equal number of items.
choices.explanation: Equal distribution is arbitrary.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Product Owner decides.
choices.explanation: The Developers select the work; the Product Owner orders the Product Backlog.

questions.question:
How often should Developers change?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: As needed, while taking into account a short term reduction in productivity.
choices.explanation: Membership can change when needed, while accepting the short-term reduction in productivity it causes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Never, because it reduces productivity.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not forbid changes; sometimes they are needed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As needed, with no special allowance for changes in productivity.
choices.explanation: Changes have a cost; ignoring the short-term productivity drop is unrealistic.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every Sprint to promote shared learning.
choices.explanation: Changing members every Sprint disrupts the team and lowers productivity.

questions.question:
Who should make sure everyone on the Developers does his or her tasks for the Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Project Manager.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Project Manager.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not supervise tasks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not manage tasks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Developers hold each other accountable as professionals.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All of the above.
choices.explanation: Only the Developers are correct.

questions.question:
When is it most appropriate for the Developers to change the Definition of Done?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: During Sprint Planning.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning focuses on selecting and planning work for the Sprint, not on inspecting and adapting the Definition of Done.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prior to starting a new Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done can evolve as the Scrum Team learns and improves, not only prior to starting a new project.

choices.label: C
