choices.text: During the Sprint Retrospective.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is where the Scrum Team inspects how it worked and adapts its practices, which can include improving the Definition of Done.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prior to starting a new project.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done can evolve as the Scrum Team learns and improves, not only prior to starting a new project.

questions.question:
As the Sprint Planning meeting progresses, the Developers see that the workload is greater than they can handle. Which two are valid actions?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recruit additional Developers before the work can begin.
choices.explanation: Hiring before starting delays the Sprint; scope should adapt instead.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers ensure that the Product Owner is aware, starts the Sprint, and monitors progress.
choices.explanation: Making the situation transparent and starting the Sprint while monitoring progress is empirical.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cancel the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint, and this is not a reason.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remove or change selected Product Backlog items.
choices.explanation: The Developers and the Product Owner can adjust the selected items to match capacity.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Developers work overtime during this Sprint.
choices.explanation: Overtime is unsustainable and hides the real capacity.

questions.question:
Currently, your Developers are organized to address a single layer only (for example, front end, middle tier, back end, and interfaces). What are three things to consider when deciding to move away from such component teams toward feature teams?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: You cannot do Scrum without feature teams.
choices.explanation: Scrum can be started with component teams; feature teams are preferable but not a prerequisite.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Productivity may suffer when making this kind of move.
choices.explanation: Reorganizing teams usually reduces productivity in the short term.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Getting support from the business side first helps.
choices.explanation: Business support helps to sustain the change.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Feature teams have less communication overhead.
choices.explanation: Feature teams reduce dependencies and communication overhead between teams.

choices.label: E
choices.text: With feature teams, it is easier to calculate the productivity per team.
choices.explanation: Comparing productivity per team is not a goal.

questions.question:
During a Sprint, when is new work or further decomposition of work added to the Sprint Backlog?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the Product Owner identifies new work.
choices.explanation: The Developers own the Sprint Backlog; the Product Owner does not add work to it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: As soon as possible after they are identified.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog is updated throughout the Sprint as more is learned, as soon as new work is identified.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the Scrum Master has time to enter them.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not maintain the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: During the Daily Scrum after the Developers approve them.
choices.explanation: Developers do not have to wait for the Daily Scrum or an approval to update their plan.

questions.question:
What is the main reason for the Scrum Master to be at the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: To gather status and progress information to report to management.
choices.explanation: Status reporting to management is not the purpose of the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To write down any changes to the Sprint Backlog, including adding new items, and tracking progress on the burn-down.
choices.explanation: The Developers maintain the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He or she does not have to be there; he or she only has to ensure the Developers have a Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master only ensures the Daily Scrum takes place; attendance is not required.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To make sure every team member answers the three questions.
choices.explanation: The three questions are not mandatory.

questions.question:
You have six teams using a traditional method to deliver a product. Your management has asked you to start using Scrum. In the initial project there were separate plans and teams for the layers of a software system, i.e. one for the frontend, one for the middle tier, one for the back-end, and one for the interfaces and services. This resembles what is known as component teams. But you have read that it's a good idea to have teams organized by feature. What are the advantages of keeping component teams while starting Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: There's less initial disruption than organizing into new teams. As they start, they will discover what works best, and how to potentially re-organize towards this.
choices.explanation: Starting with existing teams causes less disruption; they can then discover how to reorganize.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Component teams generally have the skills needed to create a working Increment of software that provides business value.
choices.explanation: Component teams usually cannot create a working Increment alone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because they have worked together for some time, they are likely able to start producing shippable Increments faster that new feature teams would.
choices.explanation: Component teams usually need integration, so they do not deliver shippable Increments faster.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There are fewer cross-team dependencies than working in feature teams.
choices.explanation: Component teams typically have more cross-team dependencies.

questions.question: True or False: A properly functioning Scrum Team will have at least one Release Sprint and may well have several.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Release Sprints do not exist in Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Every Sprint produces a usable Increment; there is no Release Sprint.

questions.question: True or False: Scrum is a methodology that tells in detail how to build software incrementally.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Scrum is a framework, not a detailed methodology.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Scrum is intentionally incomplete; it does not tell in detail how to build software.

questions.question:
For which is the Scrum Master responsible?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Managing the performance of the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not manage performance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The meetings and the objectives that a Scrum Team sets for itself.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team sets its own objectives.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum framework being adopted and used properly.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is accountable for establishing Scrum as defined in the Scrum Guide.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keeping track of resource allocation.
choices.explanation: Resource allocation is not a Scrum Master responsibility.

questions.question:
The Developers asks their Product Owner to re-order the Product Backlog. The team is waiting for an external supplier to deliver a specific software component. Without that component there won't be enough work in the next Sprint to occupy the full team. The Product Owner asks the Scrum Master for help. What would be good advice to give the Product Owner?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Remind the Product Owner that his primary concern is the flow of value reflected in the ordering of the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: This aligns the ordering decision with value delivery, which is the Product Owner’s responsibility.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tell the Product Owner to re-order the Product Backlog so the work involving the external component can be planned in a separate sprint.
choices.explanation: This focuses on scheduling around the supplier component rather than advising on ordering for value delivery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tell the Product Owner that the Product Backlog should be ordered to maximize utilization of the Developers.
choices.explanation: Ordering to keep people busy prioritizes utilization over delivering the most valuable outcomes.

questions.question:
What are three ways Scrum promotes self-management?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: By not allowing documentation.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not forbid documentation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: By the Developers deciding what work to do in a Sprint.
choices.explanation: Developers select the work for the Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: By preventing stakeholders from entering the development room.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders are not prevented from interacting with the team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: By removing titles for Developers.
choices.explanation: Scrum recognizes no titles for Developers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: By being a lightweight framework.
choices.explanation: Scrum is lightweight, leaving room for the team to decide how to work.

questions.question:
What is the key concern when multiple Scrum Teams are working from the same Product Backlog?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Minimizing dependencies between teams.
choices.explanation: Minimizing dependencies between teams is the key concern.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clear definition of requirements.
choices.explanation: Requirements emerge; clear definition is not the key concern.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Meeting original scope projections.
choices.explanation: Original scope is not fixed in Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Making sure there's enough work for everyone on every team.
choices.explanation: Keeping people busy is not a goal.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Maximizing velocity.
choices.explanation: Velocity is not a goal.

questions.question:
What does it mean to say that an event has a time-box?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The event must happen at a set time.
choices.explanation: A timebox refers to duration, not to the scheduled start time of the event.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The event must happen by a given time.
choices.explanation: A timebox limits how long the event can last, not when it must be completed by.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The event must take at least a minimum amount of time.
choices.explanation: A timebox sets an upper limit, not a required minimum duration.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The event can take no more than a maximum amount of time.
choices.explanation: A timebox establishes a maximum duration that the event cannot exceed.

questions.question:
Which outcome is expected as Scrum Teams mature?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: They will improve their Definition of Done to include more stringent criteria.
choices.explanation: As teams mature, their Definition of Done is expected to include more stringent criteria for higher quality.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Sprint Retrospectives will grow to be longer than 4 hours.
choices.explanation: Retrospectives remain timeboxed to three hours maximum for a one-month Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There is no need for a time-boxed Sprint, since time-boxes are only for new Scrum Teams.
choices.explanation: Timeboxes apply to all Scrum Teams, mature or not.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sprint Reviews will no longer be needed.
choices.explanation: Sprint Reviews are always needed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A Scrum Master is no longer needed since they are a mature team now.
choices.explanation: A Scrum Master is always part of a Scrum Team.

questions.question:
Five new Scrum Teams have been created to build one product. A few of the Developers on one of the Scrum Teams ask the Scrum Master how to coordinate their work with the other teams. What should the Scrum Master do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Teach the Product Owner to work with the lead Developers on ordering Product Backlog in a way to avoid too much technical and development overlap during a Sprint.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no lead Developers, and ordering does not replace coordination.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Teach them that it is their responsibility to work with the other teams to create an integrated Increment.
choices.explanation: The Developers are responsible for working with the other teams to create an integrated Increment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Collect the Sprint tasks from the teams at the end of their Sprint Planning and merge that into a consolidated plan for the entire Sprint.
choices.explanation: Consolidating plans is centralized control.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Visit the five teams each day to inspect that their Sprint Backlogs are aligned.
choices.explanation: Daily inspection by the Scrum Master is control, not coaching.

questions.question:
Who must attend the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master and Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master and Product Owner are not required.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is the Developers' event.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers and Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is not required.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Only the Developers are required, not the whole Scrum Team.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Developers and Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is not required.

questions.question:
In the Sprint Planning meeting, the Product Owner and the Developers were unable to reach a clear understanding about the highest order Product Backlog items. Because of this, the Developers couldn't figure out how many Product Backlog items it could forecast for the upcoming Sprint. They were able to agree on a Sprint Goal, however. Which of the following two actions should the Scrum Master support?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cancel the Sprint. Send the entire team to an advanced Scrum training and then start a new Sprint.
choices.explanation: Cancelling the Sprint is not appropriate, and only the Product Owner can cancel.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Forecast the most likely Product Backlog items to meet the goal and create a Sprint Backlog based on a likely initial design and plan. Once the time-box for the Sprint Planning meeting is over, start the Sprint and continue to analyze, decompose, and create additional functionality during the Sprint.
choices.explanation: With a Sprint Goal, the Developers can forecast the likely items, start, and refine during the Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continue the Sprint Planning meeting past its time-box until an adequate number of Product Backlog items are well enough understood for the Developers to make a complete forecast. Then start the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is timeboxed; it cannot be extended.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Discuss in the upcoming Sprint Retrospective why this happened and what changes will make it less likely to recur.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective is the place to understand why this happened and improve.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ask everyone to take as much time as needed to analyze the Product Backlog first, and then reconvene another Sprint Planning meeting.
choices.explanation: Postponing planning delays the Sprint; Sprints follow each other without gaps.

questions.question:
Which answer best describes the topics covered in Sprint Planning?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: What to do and who will do it.
choices.explanation: Developers self-manage; who does what is not decided at Sprint Planning.

choices.label: B
choices.text: How conditions have changed and how the Product Backlog should evolve.
choices.explanation: Adapting the Product Backlog to changes is a Sprint Review topic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: What can be done and how to do it.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning addresses what can be Done and how, along with why the Sprint is valuable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: What went wrong in the last Sprint and what to do differently this Sprint.
choices.explanation: Looking back is the Sprint Retrospective.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Who is on the team and what team member roles will be.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning does not define roles.

questions.question:
Which of the following is required by Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sprint Retrospective.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is a mandatory Scrum event.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Members must stand up at the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: Standing up is a common practice, but not required by Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sprint Burndown Chart.
choices.explanation: Burn-down charts are optional.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release planning.
choices.explanation: Release planning is not part of Scrum.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All of the above.
choices.explanation: Since only the Sprint Retrospective is required, this answer is wrong.

questions.question:
How should the Developers deal with non-functional requirements?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ensure every Increment meets them.
choices.explanation: Non-functional requirements apply to every Increment, typically via the Definition of Done.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Make sure the release department understands these requirements, but it is not the Developers' responsibility.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team is responsible for all product-related activities, including non-functional requirements.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Handle them during the Integration Sprint preceding the Release Sprint.
choices.explanation: There is no Integration Sprint or Release Sprint in Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assign them to the lead Developers on the team.
choices.explanation: There is no Lead Developer in Scrum; Developers share accountability.

questions.question:
When is a Sprint over?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the Product Owner says it is done.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not end the Sprint arbitrarily.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When all Product Backlog items meet their Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: The Sprint does not end when items are done; it is timeboxed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When all the tasks are completed.
choices.explanation: Completing tasks does not end the Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the time-box expires.
choices.explanation: A Sprint ends when its timebox expires.

questions.question: True or False: Scrum has a role called "Project Manager".

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Project Manager role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Scrum defines only Product Owner, Scrum Master and Developers.

questions.question:
How much time is required after a Sprint to prepare for the next Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The break between Sprints is time-boxed to 1 week for 30 day Sprints, and usually less for shorter sprints.
choices.explanation: There is no break between Sprints.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enough time for the requirements for the next Sprint to be determined and documented.
choices.explanation: Refinement happens during the Sprint; no extra time is needed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enough time for the Developers to finish the testing from the last Sprint.
choices.explanation: Testing is done within the Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: None. A new Sprint starts immediately following the end of the previous Sprint.
choices.explanation: A new Sprint starts immediately after the previous one ends.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All of the above are allowed depending on the situation.
choices.explanation: None of these breaks are allowed.

questions.question:
When many Scrum Teams are working on the same product, should all of their Increments be integrated every Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, but only for Scrum Teams whose work has dependencies.
choices.explanation: All teams working on the same product contribute to one integrated Increment, dependencies or not.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, otherwise the Product Owners (and stakeholders) may not be able to accurately inspect what is done.
choices.explanation: Integration is needed every Sprint to inspect what is really done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No, each Scrum Team stands alone.
choices.explanation: Teams on one product do not stand alone.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, that is far too hard and must be done in a hardening Sprint.
choices.explanation: Hardening Sprints do not exist in Scrum.

questions.question:
Which output from Sprint Planning provides the Developers with a target and overarching direction for the Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Sprint Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog contains selected work and a plan, but not the overarching direction itself.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Sprint Goal
choices.explanation: The Sprint Goal provides the target and overarching direction for the Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The release plan.
choices.explanation: A release plan is not an official Scrum output of Sprint Planning.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sprint Review minutes.
choices.explanation: Sprint Review minutes are not an output of Sprint Planning.

questions.question:
During the Sprint Retrospective a Scrum Team has identified several high priority process improvements. Which of the following statements is most accurate?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Team may add items to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Guide says the most impactful improvements may be added to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint; it is a choice of the Scrum Team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Team should choose at least one high priority process improvement to place in the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: There is no obligation to place an improvement in the Product Backlog.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Team should decline to add a process improvement to the Sprint Backlog when things are running smoothly.
choices.explanation: Continuous improvement remains valuable even when things go well.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master selects the most important process improvement and places it in the Sprint Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not decide for the Scrum Team which improvements to take.

questions.question:
Who is accountable for clearly expressing Product Backlog items?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The business analyst who represents the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The work can be delegated, but the Product Owner remains accountable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for creating and clearly communicating Product Backlog items, even if delegated.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Master, or the Scrum Master may have the Developers do it.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is not accountable for Product Backlog items, nor does the work shift accountability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master helps but is not accountable for Product Backlog items.

questions.question:
When many Scrum Teams are working on a single product, what best describes the Definition of Done?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Each Scrum Team defines and uses its own. The differences are discussed and reconciled during a hardening Sprint.
choices.explanation: Hardening Sprints do not exist in Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Masters from each Scrum Team define a common Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done is set by the Scrum Teams, not by the Scrum Masters.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each Scrum Team uses its own, but must make their definition clear to all other teams so the differences are known.
choices.explanation: Separate definitions do not guarantee that the combined work is releasable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All Scrum Teams must have a Definition of Done that makes their combined work potentially releasable.
choices.explanation: Teams on the same product share a Definition of Done ensuring their integrated work is releasable.

questions.question:
At the seventh Sprint Review, the stakeholders are disappointed and angry. They have determined that the product or system being built will not meet their needs and will cost more than they are willing to spend. What factors likely led to this?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Project Management Office (PMO) has not been engaged adequately.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no PMO role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner has not been keeping the stakeholders aware of the progress of the project.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner should keep stakeholders informed about progress.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The stakeholders haven't been using the Sprint Reviews to inspect and evaluate progress.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders should use Sprint Reviews to inspect progress.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The stakeholders were not allowed to enter the development area.
choices.explanation: Access to the development area is not the issue.

questions.question:
As the Scrum Team starts work during the Sprint, it realizes it has selected too much work to finish in the Sprint. What should it do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inform the Product Owner at the Sprint Review, but prior to the demonstration.
choices.explanation: Waiting until the Sprint Review delays necessary adaptation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Find another Scrum Team to give the excess work to.
choices.explanation: Work is not reassigned to other teams mid-Sprint to handle overcommitment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As soon as possible in the Sprint, work with the Product Owner to remove some work or Product Backlog items.
choices.explanation: Developers and the Product Owner collaborate to adjust scope while preserving the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduce the Definition of Done and get all of the Product Backlog items "Done" by the new definition.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done cannot be lowered to accommodate more work.

questions.question:
Which two activities will a Product Owner engage in during a Sprint?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is the Developers' event.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prioritize the Developers' work on the Sprint Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Developers manage the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Update management on what is being worked on.
choices.explanation: Reporting to management is not a specific Product Owner activity in Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Answer questions from the Developers about items in the current Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner answers questions about items in the Sprint.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Work with the stakeholders.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner works with stakeholders to maximize value.

questions.question:
What are two good ways for the Developers to make non-functional requirements visible?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Put them on a separate list on the Scrum board, available for all to see.
choices.explanation: A separate list fragments the work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add them to the Product Backlog and keep the Product Owner posted on the expected effort.
choices.explanation: Adding them to the Product Backlog makes them transparent and orderable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Run the integration and regression tests before the end of the Sprint, and capture the open work for the Sprint Backlog of the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: Deferring work creates undone work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add them to the Definition of Done so the work is taken care of every Sprint.
choices.explanation: Adding them to the Definition of Done ensures they are met every Sprint.

questions.question:
Which three questions might be answered by Developers at the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: How is the Sprint proceeding?
choices.explanation: This is a general question, not one of the three classic questions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: What did I do yesterday that helped the Developers meet the Sprint Goal?
choices.explanation: The classic question about yesterday's progress toward the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Why were you late?
choices.explanation: This is not a valid Daily Scrum question.

choices.label: D
choices.text: What will I do today to help the Developers meet the Sprint Goal?
choices.explanation: The classic question about today's work toward the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: E
choices.text: How many hours did I spend on the project yesterday?
choices.explanation: Hours spent are not tracked in Scrum.

choices.label: F
choices.text: What will I be working on tomorrow?
choices.explanation: The question is about today, not tomorrow.

choices.label: G
choices.text: Do I see any impediment that prevents me or the Developers from meeting the Sprint Goal?
choices.explanation: The classic question about impediments to the Sprint Goal.

questions.question:
When does a Developer become accountable for the value of a Product Backlog item selected for the Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: During the Daily Scrum
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum does not assign individual accountability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whenever a team member can accommodate more work.
choices.explanation: Capacity does not create individual accountability for value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Never. The entire Scrum Team is accountable for creating value every Sprint.
choices.explanation: The entire Scrum Team is accountable for creating a valuable, useful Increment every Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At the Sprint Planning Event.
choices.explanation: Selecting items at Sprint Planning does not make an individual accountable for value.

questions.question:
Which best describes the Product Backlog?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is allowed to grow and change as more is learned about the product and its customers.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is emergent; it grows and changes as more is learned.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It provides just enough information to enable a Scrum team to start the design phase of a product.
choices.explanation: There is no design phase in Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It contains all foreseeable tasks and requirements from which the Scrum team can develop and maintain a complete project plan.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is never complete.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is baselined to follow change management processes.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is never baselined.

questions.question:
Who has the final decision about the order of items in the Product Backlog?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders influence the Product Owner, but they do not decide the order.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for Product Backlog management, including ordering; the organization must respect their decisions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team contributes to refinement, but the final say on ordering belongs to the Product Owner.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master helps the Product Owner but does not decide the order.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers can be asked to help, but the Product Owner remains accountable for the order.

questions.question:
What is the accountability of the Product Owner during Sprint 0?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: There is no such thing as Sprint 0.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Sprint 0.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gathering, eliciting, and analyzing the requirements that will be inserted into the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: There is no Sprint 0; the Product Backlog emerges.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Make the complete project plan to commit date, budget, and scope to the stakeholders.
choices.explanation: There is no Sprint 0 nor fixed upfront plan.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Determine the composition of the Developers so they have the capacity to deliver the completed forecast.
choices.explanation: Team composition is not the Product Owner's accountability.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Make sure enough Product Backlog items are refined to fill the first 3 Sprints.
choices.explanation: There is no Sprint 0.

questions.question:
In accordance with Scrum theory, how should a group of 100 people be divided into multiple Scrum Teams?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Understanding the product, the product vision and the rules of the Scrum framework, the group divides itself into teams.
choices.explanation: Scrum promotes self-managing teams; people who understand the product and Scrum framework organize themselves into appropriate teams.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It doesn't really matter because you can rotate the teams every Sprint to spread knowledge.
choices.explanation: Rotating teams every Sprint reduces stability and undermines team cohesion, which Scrum relies on for effectiveness.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Check with the allocation department to see who has worked together before and make these the first teams.
choices.explanation: Using an external allocation department to decide team composition conflicts with Scrum’s principle of self-management.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a matrix of skills, seniority, and level of experience to assign people to teams.
choices.explanation: Assigning people based on a management-designed skills matrix contradicts Scrum’s emphasis on self-managing, cross-functional teams.

questions.question:
Who is accountable for tracking the remaining work toward the Sprint Goal?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Developers are accountable for managing and tracking progress toward the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master facilitates Scrum but is not accountable for tracking remaining Sprint work.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing product value, not tracking remaining Sprint work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Project Manager.
choices.explanation: The Project Manager role is not defined in Scrum and does not track Sprint work.

questions.question:
When must a Product Owner release each Increment?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: When it makes sense.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner decides to release when it makes sense.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the Scrum Team finishes their work.
choices.explanation: Finishing work does not trigger a release.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whenever the product is free of defects.
choices.explanation: A product is rarely free of defects; that is not the release criterion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: After every Sprint, Without exception.
choices.explanation: Releasing is not mandatory every Sprint.

questions.question:
What are two good ways for a Scrum Team to ensure security concerns are satisfied?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Postpone the work until a specialist can perform a security audit and create a list of security-related Product Backlog items.
choices.explanation: Postponing creates undone work and risk; security should be addressed continuously.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add security concerns to the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: Adding security criteria to the Definition of Done ensures every Increment meets them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add a Sprint to specifically resolve all security concerns.
choices.explanation: There is no special-purpose Sprint in Scrum; every Sprint should produce a usable Increment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Delegate the work to the concerned department.
choices.explanation: Delegating outside the Scrum Team removes ownership; the Scrum Team should have the skills, or acquire them, to address security.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Have the Scrum Team create Product Backlog items for each concern.
choices.explanation: Specific security concerns can be made transparent as Product Backlog items and ordered by the Product Owner.

questions.question:
What is the recommended size for a Scrum Team?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least 7.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not set a minimum of 7.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require exactly 9.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 10 or fewer.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team is typically 10 or fewer people.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 7 plus or minus 3.
choices.explanation: This is an old rule; the current Scrum Guide says 10 or fewer.

questions.question:
Select two ways in which technical debt impacts transparency.
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: When calculated and estimated, the total amount of technical debt shows exactly how long until the Product Owner can release the Increment.
choices.explanation: Technical debt does not tell when the Increment can be released.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It leads to false assumptions about the current state of the system, specifically of an Increment being releasable at the end of a Sprint.
choices.explanation: Technical debt creates false assumptions about the state of the system.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As development progresses and code is added, the system becomes more difficult to stabilize, which results in future work being slowed down in unpredictable ways.
choices.explanation: Technical debt slows future development unpredictably.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It enhances transparency for the Product Owner as the Developers are not allowed to do additional feature development in a Sprint as long as there is technical debt.
choices.explanation: Technical debt does not enhance transparency, and Developers are not prevented from feature development.

questions.question:
The Developers are required to deliver a done Increment by the end of a Sprint. Select two statements that explain what "Done" means.
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: All work the Developers are willing to do.
choices.explanation: Done is not about willingness; it is defined by the Definition of Done.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ready for integration.
choices.explanation: Ready for integration is not Done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No work left from the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: Done means meeting all criteria of the Definition of Done.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whatever the Product Owner defines as quality.
choices.explanation: Quality is defined by the Definition of Done, not by the Product Owner alone.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All work to create software that is ready to be released to end users.
choices.explanation: Done means the Increment is usable and could be released.

questions.question:
Which of the following are true about the length of the Sprint?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The length of the Sprint should be proportional to the work that is done in between Sprints.
choices.explanation: There is no work between Sprints.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is best to have Sprints of consistent length throughout a development effort.
choices.explanation: Sprint length is not decided per Sprint, and testing is included.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sprint length is determined during Sprint Planning, and should hold the time it will take to code the planned features in the upcoming Sprint, but does not include time for any testing.
choices.explanation: Sprints have a consistent length; scope adapts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sprint length is determined during Sprint Planning, and should be long enough to make sure the Developers can deliver what is to be accomplished in the upcoming Sprint.
choices.explanation: Sprints of consistent length create rhythm and predictability.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All Sprints must be 1 month or less.
choices.explanation: Sprints are one month or less.

questions.question:
Developers include which role(s)?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: No other roles. Developers is one of the 3 accountabilities in Scrum.
choices.explanation: Developers is one of the three accountabilities; Scrum recognizes no sub-roles.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Testers.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no tester role.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Business Analysts.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no business analyst role.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Software Architects.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no architect role.

questions.question:
The Sprint Backlog must be detailed enough that...
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: every task is identified when the Sprint Backlog is first created.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog emerges; not every task is known at first.

choices.label: B
choices.text: changes in progress can be understood in the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog must be detailed enough to inspect progress at the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the Product Owner can understand what everyone is working on.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog is for the Developers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: stakeholders can monitor progress at task level.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders do not monitor tasks.

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Master is accountable for the Product Backlog.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is not accountable for the Product Backlog.

questions.question: True or False: A Scrum Team uses 2 weeks Sprints and time box their Sprint Planning to 6 hours. Does this break the rules of Scrum?

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Six hours stays within the eight-hour maximum, so it does not break the rules.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is at most eight hours for a one-month Sprint; six hours for two weeks is allowed.

questions.question:
Who is accountable for ensuring that the burn-down chart and gantt chart exist?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: No one.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require burndown or Gantt charts, so no one is accountable for them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Developers may use a burndown if they wish, but Scrum does not require it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner may use projective practices, but no specific chart is required.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is not accountable for any chart; Scrum requires none.

questions.question: True or False: By the end of the Sprint Retrospective, the Scrum Team should have identified and planned improvements to increase its effectiveness.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective identifies improvements to increase quality and effectiveness.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The purpose of the Retrospective is to plan improvements.

questions.question:
The Scrum Master is a leader and servant in service to which of the following?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The organisation and Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team and the organization.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master serves the Product Owner, but not only.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master serves the Developers, but not only.

questions.question:
The Product Owner manages...
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: the Developers.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not manage the Developers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team is self-managing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the Project.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no project management role.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.

questions.question:
Management need to monitor progress on a daily basis and decide to do so by attending the Daily Scrum. What are the likely results?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Management will be able to better direct the work of the Developers.
choices.explanation: Management does not direct the Developers' work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Additional facilitation may be required to keep to the time-box.
choices.explanation: Additional people may require facilitation to stay within the timebox.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Developers may end up with less time in the Daily Scrum to re-plan their work.
choices.explanation: Management attendance takes time away from re-planning.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Developers may be less open and transparent during the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The presence of management may make Developers less open.

questions.question: True or False: The Product Owner must attend the Sprint Retrospective.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is a Scrum Team member and attends the Retrospective.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective is a Scrum Team event, including the Product Owner.

questions.question: True or False: A Scrum Team must only work on a single Product Goal at any time.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team must fulfil or abandon one Product Goal before taking on the next.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Guide says there is one Product Goal at a time.

questions.question: True or False: The Definition of Done is a mandatory part of Scrum.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done is the commitment for the Increment, mandatory in Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done is mandatory.

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Master must facilitate the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master ensures the Daily Scrum takes place, but does not have to facilitate it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Developers run their Daily Scrum.

questions.question:
Among the Developers, there is nobody with significant testing expertise. They should...
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: request for a specialist tester to join them and queue testing for them to do when they arrive in a later Sprint.
choices.explanation: Queuing testing for a later Sprint creates undone work; each Increment must meet the Definition of Done.

choices.label: B
choices.text: produce an Increment that will be tested by a dedicated test team after the Sprint to guarantee the quality.
choices.explanation: Testing after the Sprint by a separate team means the Increment is not Done; quality is built in by the Developers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: raise this as an impediment which may require the assistance of the Scrum Master to resolve.
choices.explanation: A missing skill can be raised as an impediment; the Scrum Master helps cause its removal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: quality is the responsibility of the Developers and they should undertake testing themselves to the best of their abilities.
choices.explanation: The Developers are accountable for quality and test as well as they can, while building the missing skills.

questions.question: True or False: The Sprint Planning event is comprised of 2 parts and the Product Owner is not needed at the 2nd part.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is not split; the whole Scrum Team collaborates throughout.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner participates in the whole Sprint Planning.

questions.question:
Product Backlog refinement is...
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: carried out once per Sprint.
choices.explanation: Refinement is ongoing, not a once-per-Sprint activity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: a Scrum event.
choices.explanation: Refinement is not a Scrum event.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the concern of the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: Refinement is a collaboration, not only the Product Owner's concern.

choices.label: D
choices.text: an ongoing process in which the Product Owner and the Developers collaborate.
choices.explanation: Refinement is an ongoing activity in which the Product Owner and Developers collaborate.

questions.question:
An Increment is...
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: all work that has happened up to the current point in time.
choices.explanation: An Increment only includes Done work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: all work completed up to now, where there are no bugs present.
choices.explanation: Bug-free is not the definition; the Definition of Done is.

choices.label: C
choices.text: all work that was carried out in the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Work carried out but not Done is not part of the Increment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the sum of the Done work during a Sprint, plus the work Done in earlier Sprints.
choices.explanation: An Increment is additive: it includes all prior Increments plus the new Done work.

questions.question:
The result of the Sprint Review is...
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: incomplete Product Backlog Items have been reviewed and returned to the top of the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Incomplete items return to the Product Backlog, but that is not the main result.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the Increment has been demonstrated to Stakeholders.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review is not just a demo.

choices.label: C
choices.text: a revised Product Backlog that defines the probable Product Backlog items for the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review results in a revised Product Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: acceptance (or rejection) of all Product Backlog Items.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review is not a formal acceptance.

questions.question:
The Product Owner is using burn-up charts instead of burn-down charts. What would your response be as Scrum Master?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: There's nothing wrong with it.
choices.explanation: Burn-up charts are a valid practice; Scrum does not prescribe any chart.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Burn-up charts are used in traditional methods and should be replaced by burn-down charts.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not prescribe burndown charts.

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Master manages the Scrum Team.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master serves and coaches the Scrum Team; they do not manage it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team is self-managing.

questions.question:
A Scrum Team has how many specific accountabilities?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: One is too few: Scrum defines three accountabilities.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: There is no fourth accountability such as a Project Manager.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Two is too few: the Developers, the Product Owner and the Scrum Master are all needed.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Scrum defines three accountabilities: Product Owner, Scrum Master and Developers.

questions.question: True or False: During Sprint Planning, every task must be estimated so the Developers can be sure they have the capacity to complete them in the Sprint.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Not every task must be estimated; the Sprint Backlog emerges.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require task estimates at Sprint Planning.

questions.question:
The Daily Scrum is consistently taking longer than 15 minutes. Which statement best describes what should be done?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 2nd Daily Scrum should be held at the end of the day.
choices.explanation: Adding a second Daily Scrum is not a solution.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Master should help the Developers understand why the 15 minute time-box should be respected and help them find ways to do it as required.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master helps the Developers understand the timebox and find ways to respect it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Developers should leave at the end of the 15 minutes.
choices.explanation: Leaving abruptly does not address the root cause.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Developers should take the additional time that they need in the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The timebox must be respected.

questions.question: True or False: A Scrum Team must be 10 or fewer people.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Guide says 'typically 10 or fewer', not a strict rule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team is typically 10 or fewer people, but this is not an absolute rule.

questions.question: True or False: A Scrum Team must never have any technical debt.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Technical debt exists in most products; it must be managed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not forbid technical debt; it must be made transparent and managed.

questions.question: True or False: During Sprint Planning, all Product Backlog Items must be decomposed to a definitive set of tasks for the Developers to complete.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Items do not need to be fully decomposed at Sprint Planning.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog emerges during the Sprint.

questions.question: True or False: Developers should be set stretch goals by the Product Owner as part of Sprint Planning.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Developers decide how much work they can take.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Stretch goals imposed by the Product Owner are not part of Scrum.

questions.question: True or False: During the Daily Scrum, the Developers must answer the "3 questions".

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The three questions are no longer required.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Developers choose the structure of their Daily Scrum.

questions.question:
Select the correct timebox for each Scrum event.
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sprint Planning - 8 hours, Daily Scrum - 30 minutes, Sprint Review - 4 hours, Sprint Retrospective - 3 hours.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is 15 minutes, not 30.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sprint Planning - 4 hours, Daily Scrum - 15 minutes, Sprint Review - 4 hours, Sprint Retrospective - 4 hours.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is 8 hours and the Retrospective 3 hours.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sprint Planning - 4 hours, Daily Scrum - 15 minutes, Sprint Review - 8 hours, Sprint Retrospective - 4 hours.
choices.explanation: Sprint Review is 4 hours, not 8.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sprint Planning - 8 hours, Daily Scrum - 15 minutes, Sprint Review - 4 hours, Sprint Retrospective - 3 hours.
choices.explanation: These are the correct maximum timeboxes for a one-month Sprint.

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Master can be removed once Scrum is adopted.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is an accountability of every Scrum Team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is a required accountability.

questions.question:
Who can do the work to ensure the Product Backlog is refined to a state that it is useful?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Business Analyst.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no business analyst role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders contribute, but they do not refine the Product Backlog.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers, with support from the Product Owner who is still accountable for it.
choices.explanation: The Developers can do refinement work while the Product Owner stays accountable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner can do the work, or delegate it.

questions.question:
The purpose of the Sprint Review is...
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: to show Stakeholders work that is done and work that is near to completion.
choices.explanation: Only Done work is presented as part of the Increment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review inspects the outcome of the Sprint and determines future adaptations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: to review the status of the Project.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review is not a project status review.

choices.label: D
choices.text: to check what was done and not done during the Sprint.
choices.explanation: It is more than a checklist; it is a working session to adapt.

questions.question:
Who can change the Sprint Backlog during a Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not change the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Developers own and change their Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not change the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders do not change the Sprint Backlog.

questions.question:
A Product Backlog is never complete.
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: False - A complete Product Backlog should be created before starting the first Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is never complete; it emerges.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True - As long as a product exists, its Product Backlog also exists.
choices.explanation: As long as a product exists, its Product Backlog exists and evolves.

questions.question:
A new Developer joins the Scrum Team taking the total number to 11 people. As a Scrum Master, What should you do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Instruct the Developers to split into 2 teams.
choices.explanation: Instructing a split undermines self-management.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Do nothing, the Developers must fix its own issues.
choices.explanation: Doing nothing ignores a potential issue.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Instruct the Developers to split into 2 teams, they should decide the appropriate sizes.
choices.explanation: Imposing a split is not the Scrum Master's role.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Raise the increased team size as a potential issue and help the Developers decide what to do about it.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master makes the issue transparent and helps the team decide.

questions.question:
Which technique is the best way the Scrum Master can ensure that the Developers communicate effectively with the Product Owner?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Teach the Developers to talk in terms of business needs and objectives.
choices.explanation: Teaching business language is useful but not the best way.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Observe communications between them and facilitate direct collaboration.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master observes and facilitates direct collaboration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Function as a go-between for them.
choices.explanation: Being a go-between harms direct collaboration.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Teach the Product Owner about the technologies employed during the Sprints.
choices.explanation: Teaching technology is not the best way to improve collaboration.

questions.question:
Which two things should the Scrum Team do during the first Sprint?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Develop and deliver at least one piece of functionality.
choices.explanation: Every Sprint delivers at least one piece of functionality.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deliver an Increment of useful and valuable product
choices.explanation: Every Sprint delivers a valuable, useful Increment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Determine the complete architecture and infrastructure for the product.
choices.explanation: Architecture emerges; it is not determined upfront.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create the complete Product Backlog to be developed in subsequent Sprints.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is never complete.

questions.question:
Who is on the Scrum Team?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is a member of the Scrum Team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Project Manager.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team does not include a Project Manager role.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is a member of the Scrum Team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers are one of the three accountabilities on the Scrum Team.

questions.question:
The timebox for a Daily Scrum is?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: 15 minutes.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is timeboxed to 15 minutes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 15 minutes for a 4-week sprint. For shorter Sprints it is usually shorter.
choices.explanation: It is 15 minutes regardless of Sprint length.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Two minutes per person.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not define two minutes per person.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 4 hours.
choices.explanation: Four hours is the Sprint Review timebox.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The same time of day every day.
choices.explanation: This describes consistency, not a timebox.

questions.question:
The three pillars of empiricism are:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Respect For People, Kaizen, Eliminating Waste.
choices.explanation: These are Lean principles, not Scrum pillars.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Planning, Inspection, Adaptation
choices.explanation: Planning is not a pillar.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Planning, Demonstration, Retrospective
choices.explanation: These are not pillars.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inspection, Transparency, Adaptation
choices.explanation: Transparency, inspection and adaptation are the three pillars of empiricism.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transparency, Eliminating Waste, Kaizen.
choices.explanation: Eliminating waste and Kaizen are Lean concepts.

questions.question:
Upon what type of process control is Scrum based?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hybrid.
choices.explanation: Scrum is not hybrid.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Empirical.
choices.explanation: Scrum is founded on empirical process control.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Defined.
choices.explanation: Defined processes are the opposite of Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Complex.
choices.explanation: Complex describes the problem, not the process control.

questions.question:
The timebox for the Sprint Review is:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2 hours.
choices.explanation: Sprint Review is 4 hours for a one-month Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 1 day.
choices.explanation: Sprint Review is not one day.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 4 hours for a monthly Sprint. For shorter Sprints it is usually shorter.
choices.explanation: Sprint Review is at most 4 hours for a one-month Sprint, usually shorter for shorter Sprints.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 4 hours and longer as needed.
choices.explanation: The timebox cannot be exceeded.

choices.label: E
choices.text: As long as needed.
choices.explanation: Events are timeboxed.

questions.question:
Which statement best describes a Product Owner's responsibility?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keep stakeholders from distracting the Developers.
choices.explanation: Shielding Developers from stakeholders is primarily a Scrum Master concern, not the core accountability of the Product Owner.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Optimizing the value of the work the Scrum Team does.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Managing the project and ensuring that the work meets the commitments to the stakeholders.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner focuses on maximizing value, not guaranteeing commitments.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Directing the Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers are self-managing and are not directed by the Product Owner.

questions.question:
Why is the Daily Scrum held at the same time and same place?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The place can be named.
choices.explanation: Naming the place is not the reason.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rooms are hard to book and this lets it be booked in advance.
choices.explanation: Room booking is a convenience, not the reason.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The consistency reduces complexity.
choices.explanation: Holding it at the same time and place reduces complexity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner demands it.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not demand it.

questions.question: True or False: The purpose of a Sprint is to produce a valuable and useful Increment of working product.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The purpose of a Sprint is to create a valuable, useful Increment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Producing a valuable, useful Increment is the purpose of every Sprint.

questions.question:
The timebox for the Sprint Planning event is?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: 4 hours.
choices.explanation: Four hours is the Sprint Review timebox.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Monthly.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is held every Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 8 hours for a monthly Sprint. For shorter Sprints it is usually shorter.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is at most 8 hours for a one-month Sprint, usually shorter for shorter Sprints.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whenever it is done.
choices.explanation: Events are timeboxed.

questions.question:
What is the function or purpose of Management in Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Identify and remove people that are not working hard enough
choices.explanation: Management does not monitor individuals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Monitor the progress of the Developers on the Scrum Team
choices.explanation: Management does not monitor the Developers' progress.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Support the Product Owner with insights and information into high value product and system capabilities. Support the Scrum Master to encourage organizational change that fosters empiricism, self-management, bottom-up intelligence, and intelligent product delivery.
choices.explanation: Management supports the Product Owner and the Scrum Master in enabling empiricism and self-management.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Continually monitor staffing levels of the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Monitoring staffing is not management's purpose in Scrum.

questions.question:
When does a Developer become the sole owner of an item on the Sprint Backlog?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whenever a team member can accommodate more work.
choices.explanation: No individual owns items in the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the Sprint Planning event
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning does not assign ownership.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Never. All Sprint Backlog items are "owned" by the Developers on the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog belongs to the Developers collectively.

choices.label: D
choices.text: During the Daily Scrum
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum does not assign ownership.

questions.question:
An organization has decided to adopt Scrum, but management wants to change the terminology to fit with terminology already used. What will likely happen if this is done?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Without a new vocabulary as a reminder of the change, very little change may actually happen
choices.explanation: Without new vocabulary, little change may actually happen.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The organization may not understand what has changed with Scrum and the benefits of Scrum may be lost
choices.explanation: The benefits of Scrum may be lost if what changed is not understood.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Management may feel less anxious
choices.explanation: Management may feel less anxious, but that hides the change.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All of the above
choices.explanation: All these consequences can occur.

questions.question:
Which of the following are examples of a Scrum Team practicing Scrum poorly or not exhibiting traits of a self-managing Scrum Team?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers have all the skills they need to create a valuable, useful Increment
choices.explanation: Having all the necessary skills is a sign of a good Scrum Team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stakeholders attend the Daily Scrum to check on the Scrum Team's progress.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders checking progress at the Daily Scrum is a sign of poor Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers create their own Sprint Backlog, reflecting all work that is required to meet the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: Developers creating their own Sprint Backlog is a sign of good Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Developers are collaboratively selecting their own work during the Sprint
choices.explanation: Collaboratively selecting work is a sign of self-management.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Developers invite external stakeholders to the Sprint Planning to ask them how to turn a Product Backlog item into an Increment via a complete and detailed Sprint Backlog
choices.explanation: Asking outsiders how to do the work shows a lack of self-management.

choices.label: F
choices.text: The Developers are working within the boundaries of their organization's functional description and nicely handing off work from analyst to Developer to tester to integration
choices.explanation: Hand-offs between functional roles show poor cross-functionality.

questions.question:
How much work must the Developers complete for each Product Backlog item they select for a Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: All development work and at least some testing
choices.explanation: Some testing is not enough; the Definition of Done defines the full quality.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enough so that each Product Backlog item they select meets the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: Each selected item must meet the Definition of Done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Analysis, design, programming, testing and documentation
choices.explanation: Scrum does not prescribe phases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: As much as it can fit into the Sprint
choices.explanation: Work is not deferred; it is Done or returns to the Product Backlog.

questions.question:
Who should know the most about the progress toward a business objective or a release, and be able to explain the alternatives most clearly?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Owner
choices.explanation: The Product Owner knows the progress toward business objectives.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Project Manager
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Project Manager.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers
choices.explanation: Developers know the progress within the Sprint, not toward business objectives.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is not the most knowledgeable about business progress.

questions.question:
The Developers should not be interrupted during the Sprint and the Sprint Goal should remain intact. These are conditions that foster creativity, quality and productivity. Which one of the following answers is FALSE?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Owner can help clarify or optimize the Sprint when asked by the Developers.
choices.explanation: This statement is true; the Product Owner can help clarify.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers may work with the Product Owner to add or remove work if they find themselves with more or less capacity than expected.
choices.explanation: This statement is true; scope can be adjusted.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Sprint Backlog is fully formulated in the Sprint Planning event and does not change during the Sprint.
choices.explanation: This statement is false: the Sprint Backlog emerges during the Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: As a decomposition of the selected Product Backlog items, the Sprint Backlog changes and may grow as the work emerges.
choices.explanation: This statement is true; the Sprint Backlog changes as work emerges.

questions.question:
What are two ways a Scrum Master serves to enable effective Scrum Teams?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: By facilitating Developer decision-making.
choices.explanation: Facilitating decision making helps the team become more effective.

choices.label: B
choices.text: By keeping high value features high in the Product Backlog
choices.explanation: Ordering the Product Backlog is the Product Owner's accountability.

choices.label: C
choices.text: By removing impediments that hinder the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Removing impediments is a core Scrum Master service.

choices.label: D
choices.text: By starting and ending the meetings at the proper time.
choices.explanation: Timekeeping alone is not what enables effectiveness.

questions.question:
Which are characteristics of the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is facilitated by the team lead.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no team lead.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It consists of the Scrum Master asking the team for status.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is not a status meeting with the Scrum Master.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its purpose is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum inspects progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapts the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is held first thing in the morning.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is not required to be in the morning.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its location and time remain constant.
choices.explanation: It is held at the same time and place.

questions.question:
When does a Sprint conclude?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the Product Owner decides enough has been delivered to meet the Sprint Goal.
choices.explanation: The Sprint has a fixed timebox and does not end based on a decision by the Product Owner. Scope may be adjusted, but the Sprint end date remains unchanged.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the Sprint Retrospective is complete.
choices.explanation: The Sprint ends after the Sprint Retrospective, which is the final event within the Sprint timebox. This completes the Sprint’s set of Scrum events.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When all the tasks are completed by the Developers.
choices.explanation: A Sprint is not concluded by finishing tasks; tasks are an internal planning detail. The Sprint ends when its timebox expires regardless of remaining work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When all Product Backlog items meet their Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: Not all selected items must be Done for the Sprint to end; the Sprint ends at the timebox boundary. Undone work returns to the Product Backlog for future consideration.

questions.question:
Which of the following is an example of an Increment?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A plan for the overall product release.
choices.explanation: An Increment is a usable piece of the product, not a plan. Plans are artifacts or outputs of planning activities, not product value in a usable form.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A mock-up of the product marketing materials.
choices.explanation: A mock-up is typically not usable product functionality that meets the Definition of Done. An Increment must be a potentially releasable, usable product improvement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A design for the product.
choices.explanation: A design is not the product itself and is not necessarily usable or releasable. An Increment is working, done product content that adds value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A product roll-out plan.
choices.explanation: A roll-out plan describes how to release, not a done, usable product improvement. In Scrum, an Increment is the product output that could be released.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A valuable, useful set of product features.
choices.explanation: An Increment is a concrete, usable addition to the product that provides value. It represents work completed to the Definition of Done and is potentially releasable.

choices.label: F
choices.text: All of the above.
choices.explanation: Only the option that represents a usable, done product improvement qualifies as an Increment. Plans, designs, and mock-ups are not Increments on their own.

questions.question:
Who owns the Sprint Backlog?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Chief Backlog Officer.
choices.explanation: There is no such role in Scrum; Scrum defines only the Product Owner, the Scrum Master and the Developers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog, not the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not own or manage the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers; they own it and update it throughout the Sprint.

questions.question:
Which statement best describes the Sprint Backlog as outcome of the Sprint Planning?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a complete list of all work to be done in a Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog emerges during the Sprint; it is not complete at Sprint Planning.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every item has a designated owner.
choices.explanation: Items are not assigned to individuals; the Developers collectively own the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each task is estimated in hours.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require tasks or hour estimates.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the Developers' plan for the Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers: the Sprint Goal, the selected Product Backlog items and the plan for delivering them.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is ordered by the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner orders the Product Backlog, not the Sprint Backlog.

questions.question:
A Product Owner wants advice from the Scrum Master about estimating work in Scrum. Which of these is the guideline that a Scrum Master should give?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Product Backlog items must be estimated in story points.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not prescribe any estimation unit; story points are an optional practice.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estimates are made by the Developers, after clarifying the items with the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Developers who will be doing the work are responsible for the sizing; the Product Owner helps them understand the items and the trade-offs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estimates must be in relative units.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not prescribe relative units or any other unit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scrum forbids estimating.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not forbid estimating; sizing is part of Product Backlog refinement.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Estimates are made by the Product Owner, but are best checked with the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not size the work; the Developers who will do it are responsible for the sizing.
